body:
## What changed

Keep live Wasm GC locals during extern/any conversions and follow native callers across scalar relays. Previously, A.outer could hold an object containing 73, call B.relay, and return to A.inner for collection; root traversal stopped in B and A.outer returned 0. The walker now crosses validated foreign frames, skips their collector-local slots, and resumes scanning A's older roots.

AMD64 and ARM64 retain zero-root return maps for collector-free relays. Exact return PCs, physical stack bounds, register adapters, and saved instance contexts select each caller. Retained immutable imports support relays through another Runtime, including closed producers and shared code. Host callbacks publish the parked chain and suspend the public caller's collector lease. Plain numeric host calls retain their fast dispatch path.

The unused-table control already passed at parent `d329e9df9`; the earlier draft description incorrectly carried its old failure forward. The remaining native relay and host-suspension faults are fixed here. The separate `fd59548a` scalar-stop prototype is not integrated.

## Validation

- Complete normal and register-check root suites; complete checked benchmark-module suite.
- Final complete Wago normal/register-check suites and runtime-concurrency controls.
- ARM64 checked root/host/codec controls, three repetitions; RV64 parked-root/artifact/plugin controls.
- Full `just lint`, including four Staticcheck profiles, generation, vet, formatting and script tests; documentation checks.
- New forced-collection tests cover both ABIs, fresh/saved code, incompatible collectors, Tiny GC, 40 shared-code relays, retained producer closure, foreign stores and host-triggered collection. Forged collector-free root slots and safepoints reject visibly.

An extra ARM64 QEMU shared-memory wait-marker test fails identically on the unchanged parent. Its root and host-reentry subtests pass. This remains a recorded baseline failure; no assertion or timeout was relaxed. Native ARM64 thread qualification is pending.

## Cost and limits

Three-sample paired controls keep root-walk allocations at zero. Median 4,098-frame walking is 31,939 → 32,021 ns; 64-frame walking is 496.4 → 513.7 ns. Ordinary conversion/root allocation counts are unchanged. Two serial 64-callback host controls improve about 2–3%, with no allocations; these small controls are not a broad speedup claim.

A numeric relay compile costs 12.071 → 13.426 µs, +519 B and +11 allocations. Its generated code stays 437 bytes; its return maps add 33 estimated wire bytes. This repair adds no instance/state fields or machine ABI. A previously failing numeric-host relay can now allocate its lazy 23,440-byte public GC state on first GC-capable use. Larger retained graphs use overflow scratch. Known retained callers without unwind maps report a recompile error; unsupported custom lowerings retain their existing limits.

[Design, lifetime proof and measured checks](https://github.com/wago-org/wago/blob/d868ee7fb3fb8c123669a2301154da8bbcd62c8e/docs/research/pr997-root-faults-2026-10-22.md).

Keep draft pending hosted qualification and review. No independent source approval, four-second result, merge, or automatic merging is claimed. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and source inspection.
